text:
julia-eng: Quick follow-ups from today's all-hands — can someone clarify the promotion timeline and 401k eligibility for folks who joined in January? Also curious about mid-cycle promotions and retro pay. Thanks!

aisha-peopleops: Great q — short answers up front: review cycle closes Jun 30, calibration the first two weeks of July, promotions typically effective Aug 1. If a promo is approved in calibration we apply retro pay back to Jul 1. For Jan hires, the guideline is 6 months in role for promo consideration unless a manager requests an exception. CC @morgan-peopleops for benefits specifics. :sparkles:

morgan-peopleops: 401(k) and benefits notes: new hires can enroll after 30 days of employment; coverage effective the 1st of the month after enrollment completes. We match contributions per our plan doc and match vesting is pro-rated over 2 years (check handbook for exact schedule). Parental leave and most core benefits are available day 1. Link: https://handbook.redwood/company/benefits (internal). :information_source:

sam-platform: Quick leveling note — managers, when you submit calibration packets please include 2–3 concrete bullets per candidate with measurable impact (latency improvements, revenue impact, cost savings). If you want a pre-submission sanity check, book a slot in manager office hours: /book-peopleops-officehours.

ben-cto: For infra/ops folks, highlight system-level impact (throughput, cost, incident reduction). Our infra rubric differs a bit from product ICs — surface the metrics. Managers: tag me if we need cross-team context.

julia-eng: Thanks — where do we file an appeal if we disagree with outcome?

aisha-peopleops: Appeals go through the People Ops appeals form in the handbook (link above). You have two weeks from the notice to file. We offer 1:1 appeal prep sessions during office hours — sign up via the same calendar.

ben-cto: Note on comp: promotions may be leveling changes without immediate comp bumps depending on budget. We try to apply comp adjustments in the August pay cycle; small increases can be discretionary if funding allows. If a promo is mission-critical, raise it during calibration and flag for comp uplift.

morgan-peopleops: Additional benefits Qs I saw in thread: medical plan enrollment windows — new hires enroll now but coverage usually begins the 1st of the month after their 30-day waiting period finishes. Dental/vision follow same pattern. Short-term disability and parental leave are effective immediately per policy.

julia-eng: Helpful — appreciate the clarity 🙏

hr-bot: Reminder: promo paperwork cutoff for this cycle is 2026-07-15 23:59 PT. Automated reminder from People Ops.

sam-platform: One small follow — can People Ops upload two anonymized calibration packet examples (one IC, one manager-led) so managers have concrete templates?

aisha-peopleops: Yes — we'll upload templates + two anonymized examples to the handbook by EOD tomorrow and send a follow-up thread with the calendar invite for calibration sync. Also posting an FAQ doc for common edge cases (mid-cycle joiners, promotions without comp, international hires).

ben-cto: Also: if you think a promotion materially affects roadmap commitments (e.g., switching priorities), ping leadership during calibration so we can re-evaluate resourcing. :thumbsup:

julia-eng: Awesome, thank you all!

morgan-peopleops: If anyone still has questions after reviewing the docs, drop them here or DM — we'll keep the thread pinned until next week.
